title: Agent Skills: A Standard for Packaged Capabilities
content:
## Overview

**Agent Skills** (often shortened to "Claude Skills") are Anthropic's packaging format for giving Claude reusable, discoverable capabilities — a folder containing instructions, optional scripts, and metadata that an agent can load on demand rather than keeping crammed into a system prompt at all times. Anthropic launched the feature in October 2025 and published the underlying format as an open standard at `agentskills.io` on December 18, 2025, so other agent platforms could adopt it too.

---

## How a Skill Works

A skill is a directory with a manifest (name, description, trigger conditions) plus supporting files. The key design idea is **progressive disclosure**: the agent's context window only pays for a one-line description per skill until it decides a skill is relevant, at which point the full instructions load. This lets an agent have access to hundreds or thousands of skills without paying a constant context tax for all of them.

```
my-skill/
  SKILL.md        # name, description, trigger guidance, instructions
  scripts/        # optional helper scripts the skill can invoke
  references/     # optional reference docs loaded only when needed
```

This is the same mechanism behind the `Skill` tool in Claude Code: a system-reminder lists available skills by name and one-line description, and invoking one loads its full instructions into that turn.

---

## The Marketplace Ecosystem

Since the open-standard release, a layered ecosystem has formed:

- **Official directory** — Anthropic ships a small, manually curated set of skills inside Claude Code, plus a partner directory with skills built by Atlassian, Canva, Cloudflare, Figma, Notion, Ramp, Sentry, Stripe, and Zapier.
- **Community directories** — third-party catalogs index far larger sets scraped from public repos. SkillsMP alone lists roughly **1.9 million public skills** pulled from GitHub.
- **Plugin marketplaces** — more than **2,500 Claude Code plugin marketplaces** are now registered at claudemarketplaces.com, many bundling skills alongside slash commands and subagent definitions.

---

## Quality Is Uneven

With that much volume, quality varies widely. SkillsBench, an independent benchmark, analyzed 47,150 public skills and found an **average quality score of 6.2 out of 12** — most published skills are thin or poorly scoped. The same benchmark found that well-curated skills raised agent task pass rates by an average of **16.2 percentage points** over no skill at all, which is the actual case for the format: a good skill measurably helps, but the median public skill is not that.

---

## Cross-Platform Adoption

Because the spec is open, adoption has spread beyond Anthropic's own products. As of June 2026, roughly **40 skills-compatible products** are listed on the official `agentskills.io` showcase, including OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and VS Code — meaning a skill authored once can, in principle, work across multiple coding agents rather than being locked to Claude Code specifically.

---

## Why It Matters

Before Agent Skills, most "give the agent a new capability" work meant either hand-writing prompt instructions per session or building a full MCP server for anything that needed executable code. Skills sit between those: lighter-weight than an MCP server (no running process, no protocol handshake), but more structured and shareable than an ad-hoc prompt snippet. The two are complementary rather than competing — a skill's instructions can themselves tell an agent to call an MCP tool.
